drafts.title: Login: add "Forgot password?" link and reset page
drafts.description:
Users keep asking how to reset their password. Add a "Forgot password?" link under the password field on the Login screen. It opens a reset page where the user enters their email and submits it to the existing reset endpoint (UI only; the backend already exists).

Today the password field in src/pages/Login.tsx (lines 28-35) is followed only by the show/hide button.
acceptance_criteria: A "Forgot password?" link appears under the password field on Login.
The link opens a reset page with an email field and a submit button.
Submitting calls the existing reset endpoint and shows a confirmation message.
The reset page links back to Login.

drafts.title: Login: show credential errors inline under the field
drafts.description:
A wrong email or password should show an inline error in red text under the field, as in the design. Keep the top banner only for network errors.

Today src/pages/Login.tsx line 22 shows every error as a banner, and src/api/auth.ts line 7 throws the same error for any failed response, so credential and network errors cannot be told apart.
acceptance_criteria: A 401/invalid-credentials response shows red text under the password field, not a banner.
A network failure or server error still shows the top banner.
The inline error clears when the user edits the field.

drafts.title: Dashboard: date range filter for orders (7/30/90 days, custom)
drafts.description:
Add a date range filter above the orders table with last 7, 30 and 90 days and a custom range with two date pickers. Default stays 7 days.

The range is hardcoded today: src/api/orders.ts lines 8-13 (DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS = 7, fetchOrders() takes no parameter) and the caption in src/pages/Dashboard.tsx line 15. fetchOrders needs a range parameter.
acceptance_criteria: The filter offers Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days and Custom range.
Last 7 days is selected by default.
Custom range shows two date pickers; the end date cannot be before the start date.
Changing the range reloads the table with orders for that range.
The caption above the table names the selected range.

drafts.title: Dashboard: export the orders shown as CSV
drafts.description:
Add an "Export CSV" button next to the date range filter. It downloads exactly the orders currently in the table for the selected range. High priority: finance asked for it twice.

There is no export today (src/pages/Dashboard.tsx lines 12-37). Depends on the date range filter.
acceptance_criteria: An "Export CSV" button is shown next to the date range filter.
The CSV contains the same rows and columns as the table for the selected range.
The file name includes the selected date range.
The button is disabled when there are no orders.

drafts.title: Dashboard: empty state when there are no orders
drafts.description:
When there are no orders for the selected range, show an empty state with a short message instead of an empty table.

Today src/pages/Dashboard.tsx lines 26-35 map over the orders with no empty branch.
acceptance_criteria: With zero orders, the table body is replaced by a short message.
The message mentions the selected date range.
With one or more orders, the table shows as before.

drafts.title: Login: show/hide password toggle (already implemented)
drafts.description: The meeting was unsure whether the show/hide password toggle from the design exists. It does: src/pages/Login.tsx line 8 keeps showPassword state and lines 31-38 switch the input type with a Show/Hide button. Only check that it matches the design.
acceptance_criteria: The existing toggle matches the Figma design (label, placement).
